memory_update.text: LRN remains the cleanest reference asset for K-12 virtual schooling and career learning; use it as a demand and execution benchmark rather than crowding the discovery lane.
NNI should be tracked as a less obvious education infrastructure supplier because its FACTS/Nelnet Business Services exposure maps to K-12/higher-ed payment, administration, and technology rails.

LOPE is a mid-cap underfollowed pathway-services candidate where the chokepoint is licensure-sensitive healthcare/teaching/social-work program execution, student services, and university-partner operations.

ATGE maps to regulated healthcare workforce education; next layer should test whether clinical placement, accreditation, and licensure outcomes create a defensible chokepoint or merely a cyclical enrollment story.

Need a separate pass for public or formerly public pure-play K-12 curriculum, assessment, tutoring, identity/rostering, LMS, and credentialing suppliers; many relevant names appear private, acquired, or buried inside larger companies.

node: K-12 virtual schooling, career learning, and postsecondary skills pathways
summary: Expanded one supply-chain node around virtual-school operating execution and career/postsecondary pathways. The two-lane universe keeps Stride as the reference validator, then adds less obvious mid-cap assets tied to payment/admin rails, licensure-sensitive university partnerships, and healthcare workforce credential pathways. This is research mapping only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
